chunks: And the confirmation of that is what Ibrahim ibn Harun al-Hiti narrated to us in the city of Al-Salam, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abu al-Thalj narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ghalib, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Dhahali, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him):

I asked: 'Allah is the Light of the Heavens and the Earth?' He answered: 'Thus is Allah, the Mighty and High.' I asked: 'A likeness of His Light?' He answered: 'Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' I asked: 'As a niche?' He replied: 'The chest of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).' I asked: 'In which is a lamp?' He said: 'In it is the Light of Knowledge, meaning Prophethood.' I asked: 'The lamp is in a glass?' He answered: 'The knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is a chest [container] leading to the heart of Ali (peace be upon him).' I asked: 'As if it were?' He asked: 'To what do you read

I asked: 'Lit from a blessed olive-tree, neither eastern nor western?' He replied: 'That is the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him), neither Jewish nor Christian.' I asked: 'The oil whereof almost gives light though fire touches it not?' He answered: 'The knowledge almost comes out of the mouth of the learned from the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) before they even speak it.' I asked: 'Light upon light?' He said: 'An Imam (peace be upon him), one after another.'

key_terms.نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Light of the Heavens and the Earth

ai.seo_question: How does the Shia tradition interpret the components of the Verse of Light in relation to the Prophet and the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* offers a precise Isma'ili-Shia exegesis of the Verse of Light, mapping the metaphorical elements to the Prophet Muhammad, the chest of Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the transmission of divine knowledge. It highlights the concept of 'Nur ala Nur' (Light upon Light) as the continuous succession of Imams, establishing the Ahl al-Bayt as the locus of divine illumination and the source of pure, innate knowledge that shines even before speech. This interpretation reinforces the Shia doctrine of the Imamate as the essential link between God and creation, rooted in the purity of the Prophet's progeny.
